title: How to convert an annual growth rate to monthly
task: De-compound a yearly rate into its monthly equivalent — forecasts, run-rate models.

excel.note: A2 = annual rate. The 12th root, not division by 12 — compounding isn't linear.

explanation: Twelve months of growth multiply, so the monthly rate is the 12th ROOT of (1 + annual) minus one: a 12.68% year unwinds to exactly 1% per month — while naive division (12.68/12 = 1.057%) overshoots, compounding to 13.4% when reapplied. The same formula generalizes: any period conversion is (1+rate)^(periods_ratio)−1 — quarterly from annual uses 1/4, annual from daily uses 365. It's CAGR's little sibling.
